title: Console taskflow observations and wireframe iteration notes - May 2026
content:
Purpose and quick summary

This is a working doc capturing observations from 8 moderated usability sessions (mix of product engineers and early enterprise customers) focused on three common console task flows: 1) creating and pinning a model route, 2) setting up a canary rollout with traffic split, and 3) inspecting request traces and cost breakdowns for recent calls. Goal was to identify friction points, validate wireframe changes from last sprint, and surface backlog candidates.

Method and participants
- Study type: remote moderated, click-along with session playback and think-aloud. Sessions recorded and time-stamped.
- Participants: 8 total (4 internal devs, 4 customer dev/platform engineers from fintech, adtech, and healthcare)
- Tasks: create a route that pins a quantized 8-bit model; configure a canary 10% traffic split; find the offending trace for a high-latency request and determine cost per token.
- Prototype: Figma v3 taskflow (linked above).

High-level takeaways
1) Route creation feels familiar but model pinning discoverability is low. Several participants expected pinning to be on the same create page; they navigated away to model catalog then wondered if the route had been created.
2) Rollout wizard language is ambiguous around traffic split semantics. People confused 'targeted users' vs 'percent of requests' and tried to create rules based on user id before finding the traffic split slider.
3) Trace-to-cost linkage is valuable but buried. Users want a 1-click path from a trace to the specific model config and its effective token unit cost.
4) Streaming examples and request previews in the console reduced errors when present; absence increases rework.
5) Users expect a persistent contextual header while working across multi-step modals showing route name, pinned model, region, and SLA tier.

Representative quotes (verbatim where possible)
- 'I thought I already pinned the model. Why is it still using the small model?'
- 'Traffic split sounds like marketing speak. Is this percentage of users or percentage of requests?'
- 'I want to jump from a slow trace to the model version that served it, not hunt in model history.'

Detailed observations and severity
- O1: Model pin action hidden on create flow (severity: high). On create-route page the pin control is collapsed under an advanced section labeled 'model options'. 4/8 participants missed it and assumed default routing would pick latest model.
- O2: Rollout rule grammar confusion (severity: medium-high). Participants tried to express targeting rules using identities; the UI only supports request-level traffic splits and variant-based targeting. Labeling and inline help insufficient.
- O3: No direct link from trace row to model config (severity: medium). Participants clicked through multiple screens to map request -> model -> version -> quantization profile. Average time to complete this mapping: 2m45s.
- O4: Cost per token not surfaced at the request-level (severity: medium). Customers want cost visibility to make routing decisions.
- O5: Modal context lost when switching tabs (severity: low-medium). When participants navigated to model catalog from the route modal, modal state was not persisted across tabs resulting in lost input.

Wireframe fallout and proposed fixes (rapid suggestions for next sprint)
- WF1: Promote model pin control to primary create-route step. Show pinned model thumbnail with version and quantization badge. Quick link to 'select different variant' should open a right-side sheet rather than navigating away. (Owner: Priya, R&D estimate: 3 dev-days)
- WF2: Rephrase rollout wizard text to explicitly state 'percent of requests' and add a help tooltip linking to a short animated GIF. Replace ambiguous 'targeted users' label with 'user attributes (advanced)'. (Owner: Maya, estimate: 1-2 days)
- WF3: Add trace row action 'Open model context' that opens a side panel showing exact model id, version, quantization, and effective cost per token with small sampling of input/outputs. (Owner: Julian, estimate: 5 dev-days + backend index work)
- WF4: Persistent route header while modal is open; breadcrumbs show route -> step and small pill showing pinned model + region. Helps keep context when jumping to catalog. (Owner: Carlos, estimate: 2 dev-days)
- WF5: Inline streaming example playground in the create-route and rollout preview screens so users can test a short prompt and see cost/time estimate. (Owner: Product-eng pairing, estimate: 4 dev-days)
backlog_items: RI-4921: Promote model pin to primary create-route step - product+ux
RI-4922: Clarify rollout wizard labels and add tooltip GIF - ux-writing
ENG-4333: Trace row 'Open model context' side panel - backend indexing + UI
ENG-4334: Persist modal state across tabs - frontend
RI-5020: Add streaming example playground to route preview - infra
next_steps: 1) Prioritize WF1 and WF3 for next sprint planning; these unblock common customer complaints and reduce support load. 2) Create design handoff package for WF1 including component states and edge cases (error states if pinned model not available). 3) Spin up an infra spike for backend model-request indexing to support model-context lookup for traces. 4) Schedule follow-up unmoderated study focusing only on rollout wizard language changes (A/B test tooltip vs inline explanation).
notes_to_self: Check with legal on whether we can display per-request cost in the console for customers on private deployments. Confirm cost calc approach with finance so numbers shown match billing exports. Reach out to customer participant from healthcare to validate quantization badge wording.
